methodology.evidence: Directly confirmed restaurant visits only; do not promote interview leads automatically.
methodology.date: Exact visit date remains null unless verified. An assigned year is approximate, and a range is retained as a range.
methodology.awards: Awards link to their actual recipient and their actual year; later recognition does not imply historical status at time of meal.
methodology.map: Map groups experiences at approximate city centers, not exact venue entrances.
methodology.favorites: Favorites come only from explicit user preference statements, independent of restaurant awards.
methodology.musicAndDining: Attending a restaurant with live jazz does not automatically count as a distinct concert. Require a separately confirmed performance before adding a concert record.
methodology.awardFocusedCollection: Default Culture Passport Dining chapter shows only venues with verified historical Michelin inclusion or James Beard recognition of restaurant itself or chef at that restaurant. Memory-only confirmed visits are preserved but hidden by default, discoverable with a separate toggle. Recognition year may differ from dinner year.
methodology.curated: Default Culture Passport dining views show confirmed restaurants with documented Michelin Guide recognition (star, Bib, Selected, historic Plate) or directly associated James Beard awards, finalists or semifinalists. Those awards retain their recipient and year. Chef awards at unrelated restaurants or historical awards dated after a dinner may be context, not proof of qualification at the meal date. Unverified and outside-scope visits stay in archive but are hidden from curated browsing by default.
methodology.featuredExceptions: Venue-specific Michelin/JBF honors are the default inclusion criteria, but the user's express favorites Sauvage, Gunther & Co., Death & Co Denver and provisional favorite The Majestic are displayed in the primary collection despite no established qualifying award.
methodology.beverages: Stand-alone cocktail bars are type=bar, never counted as restaurants. James Beard Outstanding Bar Program includes bar semifinalists. Never borrow recognition from another location within a chain.
methodology.repeatVisits: A venue may be visited in multiple years. Each confirmed year is represented as a separate experience record with a stable unique ID, sharing one venue ID; do not manufacture precise calendar dates or collapse years into one event.
methodology.reservationEvidence: Date and party size from completed reservation screenshots are documentary evidence, not independent proof of check-in or dining. Only directly restaurant-level Michelin/JBF recognition enters the curated collection automatically. The user explicitly excluded Le Fou Frog: it must not enter any deployed venue/experience ledger, even though its date appears in private conversation uploads.
methodology.storyFirst: Memories and occasions lead publicly; exact booking data is archival supporting material. No inferred visit dates, meal details, or companions.

records.title: Mister Oso

visit.label: Denver years
visit.source: Alex confirmed visiting Mister Oso in Denver. A reservation screenshot identifies Wash Park in March 2024, but a completed booking alone does not establish the date of the visit.

records.summary: Mister Oso grew from the relaxed Latin American happy-hour spirit of Señor Bear into a tropical RiNo restaurant, then expanded to Wash Park. The original earned a Michelin Bib Gourmand, and the user's visit is remembered as part of this larger Denver story.

memory.headline: From Señor Bear to a Denver neighborhood favorite
memory.teaser: A playful Latin-inspired restaurant that grew from RiNo to Wash Park, with roots in Señor Bear and a Michelin Bib Gourmand along the way.
memory.story: What began at Señor Bear in LoHi grew into something more playful. Chef Blake Edmunds took the energy of Señor Bear’s Latin-inspired happy hours and built Mister Oso around tacos, ceviche, cocktails and a colorful, tropical atmosphere. The first Mister Oso opened in RiNo in the former Populist space in November 2019. Its popularity led to a second location in Wash Park in summer 2022. You've confirmed eating at Mister Oso, and the Wash Park restaurant appears in your reservation history. Along the way, the original restaurant earned a Michelin Bib Gourmand in 2023. The link between those neighborhoods, the food and the wider Denver dining scene is the story worth keeping.
memory.source: Direct visit confirmation, 2026-10-25; historical development verified against the chef's Michelin interview and contemporary Denver reporting.

guide.note: The original RiNo location has held a Michelin Bib Gourmand since Colorado's 2023 Guide. The Culture Passport presents Mister Oso as one brand with multiple Denver locations; a Bib is not a star.

editorial.note: Mister Oso received Bib Gourmand recognition; entry tells the brand's Denver story as a whole, while the Guide's published location is retained in provenance.

curation.reason: Original RiNo restaurant earned Michelin Bib Gourmand beginning in 2023. User confirmed a Mister Oso visit, with documentary evidence relating to Wash Park; keep one entry for the restaurant concept, not a claim that the specific meal received a distinction.
